resources.string: The 2 m version A uses two elements of 3/16″ aluminum rod on a PVC support. The author formed 1″ radius bends and connected coax to the center gap of the driven element.
Aluminum rod Ø 3/16″ (4.7625 mm)
Bend radius / nominal PVC pipe size — 1″ / 1/2″
First prototype resonance reported by the author — ≈ 145.5 MHz
Vertical model · 144 MHz · height 30′, elevation 3° — 10.7 dBi · F/B 18.6 dB · (40 − j10) Ω

Version B uses the same rod with a slightly wider frame and larger tip gaps. Its dimensions come from the separate version B drawing.
Aluminum rod Ø 3/16″ (4.7625 mm)
Bend radius — 1″ / 25.4 mm
The aluminum flat-stock alternative uses screws in slotted PVC end caps. The author increased the tip gap to 2″ for the wider stock.
1″ × 1/16″ aluminum flat stock
Suggested bend radius — ≈ 1/8″
Across-band reactance reported by the author — ±6 Ω
Vertical 146.5 MHz antenna made from AWG 10 wire. The frame uses two longitudinal PVC tubes with crosspieces, and the RG‑8X at the feedpoint carries three type 43 ferrite beads.
AWG 10 wire on a PVC frame
Nominal Schedule 40 PVC size / wire drill diameter — 1/2″ / 1/8″
Hole marks on parts C / D / F — 1 1/2″ / 2 3/8″ / 1/2″
Initial wire cuts — DE 2 × 24″ · REF ≥ 45″
Reported front-to-back — 29 dB @ 146.5 MHz · ≈35 dB @ 147 MHz
Dimensions are from the baseline 435 MHz M0 model with AWG 12 wire. The article also shows a PVC-mounted build and examines how small errors at the tips affect front-to-back ratio.
Model, AWG 12 wire

Vertical 430 MHz frame by W1CDN. Cable ties hold the copper wire on a printed support, and RG‑316 crosses the center to the driven element on the right. The author used a 5 mm tip gap and measured SWR below 2:1.
AWG 14 wire on a printed frame
Original frame and print scale (depth / width) — 433 MHz · 104% / 103%
PLA infill and tip clearance — 10% · 5 mm
Reported SWR — < 2:1
KG4JJH horizontal 6 m design. The elements use tubing and rods of several diameters. Fiberglass inserts maintain the gaps between the bent ends.
Horizontal polarization, stepped aluminum elements
SWR reported on drawing — ≤ 1.3:1 @ 50–51 MHz
KG4JJH vertical version with its own geometry and a shorter boom. The model is for 53 MHz, and the drawing gives a resonance of 52.900 MHz.
Vertical polarization, 52.900 MHz resonance on the drawing
SWR reported on drawing — ≤ 1.6:1 @ 52–54 MHz
The 4 m frame uses 0.83 mm enamelled copper wire. Four fiberglass spars support the corners and a fifth carries the feedpoint and coax. A wooden block holds the spars on the mast.
0.83 mm enamelled copper wire
Spreader angle in drawing — 40°
Initial SWR — ≈ 1.3:1
The 27.555 MHz 19DX348 model uses 2 mm bare copper wire. The driven element uses a 50 Ω coaxial feed with a choke. The published 5.94 dBi gain is a simulation result.
2 mm bare copper wire
Model at 27.555 MHz — 5.94 dBi · 50 Ω
The Wimpel build has two fiberglass spreaders and a side support for its 8.82 m H155 feed line. The vertical segment of that line between the elements forms part of the design.
Portable vertical frame, 8.82 m H155 feed line
Driven halves along the frame — 2 × 192 cm
Mast height / weight without mast — 10 m / 530 g
Published span at SWR ≤ 2 — 26.5–28.4 MHz
Published power and front-to-back — 100 W · 20 dB
The Vertikal build uses 147 cm fiberglass spreaders and 13.23 m of H155. Its drawing shows a 26.3–28.5 MHz span at SWR ≤ 2.
Portable vertical frame, 13.23 m H155 feed line
Driven halves along the frame — 2 × 195 cm
Spreader length / mast height / weight without mast — 147 cm / 10 m / 530 g
Published span at SWR ≤ 2 — 26.3–28.5 MHz
EA2BD’s field Moxon for 20 m hangs vertically from one telescopic mast. Light guys hold its shape. After initial measurements the author shortened each end of the PVC-insulated wire by about 8 cm.
Original model with AWG 16 wire. Lengths were adjusted on the field build.
Field build: wire / mast — 1.5 mm² / 12 m
Trim at each wire end / initial SWR — ≈ 8 cm / ≈ 4:1
W4RNL portable frame made from 5/8″ aluminum tubing. A center boom carries the elements, while detachable corners and insulating links hold the shape in the field.
5/8″ aluminum tubing

AWG 14 copper wire

AWG 14 copper wire

The compact 868 MHz frame uses 2 mm copper wire. Its printed support is integrated with a Heltec housing.
Heltec housing, 2 mm copper wire
Conductor — Ø 2 mm
G5OLD portable 10 m kit. Its printed hub holds fiberglass spreaders for the wire frame. In the field the author used an extra guy to hold the heading.
Printed parts for a lightweight field frame
Fiberglass spreaders in the field report — Ø 8.5 mm
YAMA 2.0 uses four fishing poles in a central hub. Tethers with eyelets tension the wire and trimmer line holds the tip gaps. The author shows field builds for 10 and 15 m.
Portable frame hardware for 10 and 15 m
X-hub support angle as described by the author — 140°
